_comment: Broker config template (Task 13.76.g, rewired to the module command by Task 13.76.c).
THIS FILE IS THE TRUST ANCHOR. It is the only place an executable -- a module command
or a script path -- may be named; requests carry an installer 'id' and never a path.
It MUST be writable only by Administrators, otherwise a caller who can edit it obtains
Two entry kinds, each with its own integrity control:
commandType 'module' (PREFERRED). Runs an exported command from an installed module.
There is no file hash to pin; the equivalent guarantee comes from WHERE the module
lives. trustedModuleRoots must list only admin-writable roots, because the security
property is that the unelevated caller who submits a request cannot modify code under
Program Files. The broker also enforces minimumModuleVersion, so a stale copy that
predates a fix cannot be selected, and it imports by absolute manifest path so
PSModulePath order -- which is settable per-user -- plays no part in what loads.
commandType 'script' (LEGACY). Runs a hash-pinned file, re-verified immediately before
execution. Retained for machines where the module is not installed. Prefer 'module':
a hash pin must be re-issued on every edit, and a stale pin fails every request.
Install-ATAPModuleAllUsers (Task 13.76.c), which is why this entry is now module-kind.

installers.description: Narrowly typed local parity-task version repointing (Task 14.72).
Canonical validated AllUsers module installer (plan Task 2.1, promoted by Task 13.76.c).

allowedParameters.name: ModuleName
allowedParameters._comment: Dotted module identifier only. Rejects path separators, '..', spaces, and quotes, so the value cannot escape the modules root when the installer joins it into a path.

allowedParameters.name: RequiredVersion
allowedParameters._comment: Exact version, optionally prerelease. No ranges: the installer stages into <ModulesRoot>\<Name>\<Version>, so this becomes a directory name.

allowedParameters.name: Repository
allowedParameters._comment: Closed set of known ATAP tier feeds. An open pattern would let a request point the installer at an attacker-controlled feed.

allowedParameters.name: FeedUrl
allowedParameters._comment: Feed endpoint, restricted to known ATAP hosts. Mandatory on Install-ATAPModuleAllUsers, so marking it optional here only defers the failure into parameter binding with a worse message.

allowedParameters.name: ExpectedSha256
allowedParameters._comment: Package hash the installer verifies before writing anything. Mandatory on the cmdlet: an unpinned install is not a validated install, which is the whole point of routing through this installer.

_deliberatelyNotAllowed: ModulesRoot and DeployRoot are parameters of Install-ATAPModuleAllUsers but are
ABSENT from allowedParameters on purpose. The allowlist is positive, so omitting them
means the cmdlet's own defaults apply and a request cannot set them.
Do not add them. ModulesRoot decides where the broker writes AS AN ADMINISTRATOR;
a caller who could set it could have an arbitrary directory populated from a feed,
or shadow a system module by writing into a directory that appears earlier on
PSModulePath. DeployRoot decides where the transcript and result record land, so a
caller who could set it could redirect or suppress the audit trail for their own
elevated action. Neither is something the requester has any business choosing.
